Automatically sending DATA(p) when receiving a DATA(p) could lead to an infinite ping-pong between the two participants.

The new approach matches the discovered participant to the builtin non-secure PDP writer, so it will receive the DATA(p) of the local participant in the next periodic announcement.

Fix shared-memory segment crash on port open (#6503) (#6507)

* Fix shared-memory segment crash on port open (#6503)

* Add reproducer for shared-memory segment crash on port open

check_sanity() walks the allocator free-block tree through offset pointers
stored inside the segment. When those links are inconsistent the traversal
reads unmapped memory and the process dies. The fault is not a C++
exception, so the surrounding catch(std::exception&) cannot intercept it.

The test ships disabled: it fails by design, and on platforms without SEH
handling it aborts the whole test binary rather than one case.
